laws.rule: Drivers may not use a hand-held device to type, send or read a text message while the vehicle is moving (47 O.S. 11-901d, in force since November 2015). Hands-free and voice-operated use is allowed, as is calling emergency services. Since 1 November 2025 drivers also may not use a hand-held phone or other device at all in active school zones and work zones (House Bill 2263), with the same penalties.
laws.penalty_signal: Up to US$100 (about A$142 at RBA 30 Oct 2026, A$1 = USD 0.7040); no licence points.

items.text: Oklahoma allows cannabis for licensed medical patients. A visitor holding a medical marijuana licence issued by another US state's government can apply to the Oklahoma Medical Marijuana Authority for an out-of-state (temporary) patient licence, valid for 30 days and renewable from a week before it expires; it lets the holder buy, use and grow medical marijuana in Oklahoma. Prescriptions or recommendations from out-of-state doctors are not accepted on their own.
The temporary licence costs US$100 plus a US$4.30 card fee (about A$148 in total at RBA 30 Oct 2026, A$1 = USD 0.7040), with no reduced fee for temporary patients.

Kratom (a leaf product from a Southeast Asian tree) is legal to sell in Oklahoma under rules that took effect on 1 November 2025 (Senate Bill 891): sales to anyone under 18 are banned, products must carry that warning, synthesised alkaloids are banned, and 7-hydroxymitragynine (7-OH, a strong kratom compound) may make up no more than 1% of a product's total kratom alkaloids. In September 2026 a state representative said he would file a bill to list 7-OH and related compounds as Schedule I controlled substances.
